title: As sustainability laws reshape packaging, consumer insight is a competitive advantage
summary: Quad will be at Shoptalk 2026, showing retailers how the biggest opportunity is using AI to make physical retail perform better.
body_markdown:
Brands are replacing plastic packaging to keep pace with new sustainability laws. As material changes to packaging become mandatory, producers must figure out how to do so while remaining on-brand. Luckily, newly published research from Quad1 (NYSE: QUAD) reveals that sustainable packaging changes can not only increase successful recycling outcomes, but also positively shape consumers’ brand perception.


[The study of e-commerce shoppers](https://doi.org/10.3390/su18136568) was presented this week at SPC Advance by Dr. Mengmeng Zhao, Associate Research Director at[Quad’s premarket testing group Accelerated Marketing Insights (AMI)](https://www.quad.com/solutions/intelligence/accelerated-marketing-insights) and a Path to Purchase Institute[40 Under 40 honoree](https://p2pi.com/p2pi-names-40-under-40-class-2026) . The research conducted on behalf of Seaman Paper analyzed consumer behavior and sentiment around their Vela™ packaging, a 100% paper-based alternative to traditional flexible plastic packaging. The at-home e-commerce experiment sought to understand whether the material could offer a more sustainable packaging option, and how changing such a familiar material could affect the consumer experience.


The findings were significant for the Sustainable Packaging Coalition audience:


- **


Participants’ intent to recycle was about 40% higher for paper packaging than for plastic polybags, based on their disposal choices.


- **


**Sustainable material drew more attention:** One paper package held consumers’ attention about 60% longer than the plastic package. Of the attention paid to the paper packaging, 65% focused on its sustainability messaging.


- **


**Paper packaging supported a more eco-friendly brand perception:** The percentage of participants who viewed the packaging as coming from an eco-friendly brand was about twice as high for paper as for plastic.


- **


Once consumers understood that material was 100% paper, they **described it as innovative, thoughtful and modern** ; some also associated it with a more luxurious brand image.


“The study shows sustainable alternatives can be both compliant and a positive brand experience,” said Dr. Zhao, Associate Research Director at Quad’s AMI. “The research is particularly important as the rollout of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) laws put packaging producers another step closer to a future where they bear greater responsibility for what happens to packaging at the end of its useful life. For brands navigating these laws, especially e-commerce brands whose packaging doubles as a first physical brand experience, being able to test new packaging before it goes into market is a huge competitive advantage.”


For an online purchase, packaging may be the first physical interaction a consumer has with a brand. Without a retail environment to provide context, the package itself must communicate quality, brand identity, and what the consumer should do with it after opening.


With the right marketing activation partners, brands don’t necessarily have to wait until launch to understand how consumers will respond.


Quad’s[Accelerated Marketing Insights](https://www.quad.com/solutions/intelligence/accelerated-marketing-insights) (AMI) uses premarket consumer research to help brands evaluate packaging and other marketing experiences before they enter the market. Behavioral tools such as eye tracking can reveal not simply what consumers *say* they prefer, but what they notice, how they interact with a package and whether its intended messages are understood.
